summary: A bounded cascade is a well-supported way to reduce cost while reserving stronger models for hard cases. The central engineering problem is a calibrated external trigger, not the order of model names.

points.text: Prefer observable triggers such as failed tests, schema violations, missing evidence, policy risk, disagreement, or a task-specific calibrated score. Raw self-reported confidence is usually insufficient.
Calibrate thresholds per task class and model revision using false-accept cost as well as average accuracy. High-impact tasks should escalate earlier than reversible drafting work.
Bound the number of stages, retries, tokens, elapsed time, and spend, and define a terminal safe state. A cascade without a stop rule is an expensive loop.
Record the route decision, trigger value, models and versions, intermediate artifact, final outcome, and counterfactual samples so routing quality can be re-evaluated after drift.
